title: The Subtle Art of Not Giving a F*ck
author: Mark Manson
blurb: Mark Manson argues that modern self-help has it backwards. Constantly chasing positivity and success only reminds us of what we lack. He says we all have a limited amount of attention and concern, so the real skill is choosing carefully what deserves it. Life will always bring problems. Happiness comes from picking good problems and enjoying the work of solving them. Manson takes aim at entitlement, the belief that we are special and deserve to feel good all the time. He urges us to adopt better values, take responsibility for everything in our lives even when it isn't our fault, doubt our own certainty, and treat failure as the path to growth. Finally, he argues that facing our own mortality helps us see clearly what is truly worth caring about.

lessons.t: Chasing Happiness Makes You Less Happy
lessons.b: Wanting a positive experience is itself a negative experience, so accepting the negative is what actually frees you.
issues: scene 7: The 'LOUSY' cloud is tiny, pale and far from the figure. Its label is well under 18px and unreadable, so the feeling being named and accepted is never actually shown. The left half of the stage is mostly empty. (fix: Enlarge the cloud to about 220px wide and place it just above or beside the figure's head. Raise the 'LOUSY' label to at least 20px in ink navy at full opacity. Optionally show it dissolving or shrinking as the figure moves along the arrow, to illustrate the grip loosening.)

lessons.t: Choose Your Problems, Not Problem-Free Life
lessons.b: Life is never free of problems, so happiness comes from choosing struggles you enjoy and solving them.
issues: scene 0: The amber person figure on the tallest bar merges into the bar. The body overlaps the bar top in the same colour, so the shape reads as a bottle rather than a person standing on top of a bigger problem. (fix: Raise the figure so its feet sit on the bar's top edge with a small gap. Alternatively, draw the figure in ink navy, or give the bar a different shade so the person and the bar read as separate elements.)
